newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr pauses for breath above 118 yen at Tokyo noon.
newsitem.headline: Dlr pauses for breath above 118 yen at Tokyo noon.

text.p: 0300 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT

The dollar paused for breath at just above 118.00 yen by midday on Wednesday after its overnight gains, with further rises inhibited by hedge selling by Japanese investors and exporters at around 118.30 yen.
Caution that the dollar has risen to the upperside of the range of 110-120 yen that the monetary authorities can tolerate also prevented the dollar from rising, dealers said.
"Since the dollar is near the topside of the 110-120 yen range, people are unwilling to keep buying dollars from the current level," said a dealer at a European bank.

"Meanwhile, the dollar's unexpected run-up to 118 yen overnight, despite strong selling pressure by Japanese exporters just below that point, made traders loath to sell dollars aggressively," he said.

A former Japanese vice finance minister, Makoto Utsumi, said on Tuesday that a range of 110-120 yen to the dollar is not a problem for Japan but a yen weaker than 125 yen to the greenback would be excessive.

"The dollar will still have room to advance to around 119 yen and stop-loss buying is expected at 118.50 yen, but any sharp rise above 120 yen is not in sight right now," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Tokyo.
A dealer in the finance department of a major Japanese exporter said that the company is intent on selling dollars at 119 yen actively, although it currently limits such sales.

Many traders expect Japanese monetary authorities to start talking down the dollar if it rises above 120 yen because such rises may fuel worries about renewed trade friction with the United States through rising Japanese exports.
Traders are focusing on the release of Japan's preliminary industrial output data for June and forecasts for July and August due at 0430 GMT.

Economists' predictions for industrial output ranged from a fall of 1.2 percent to a fall of 4.0 percent for June, compared with the Ministry of International Trade and Industry's (MITI) forecast of a 2.6 percent drop in manufacturers' output.

Japanese government bond yields fell, partly on rumours that the output data for June may show a fall of 4.0 percent. Dealers said a stronger-than-expected figure may spark dollar selling, although it is likely to be supported at 117.50 yen.
Elsewhere, the Australian dollar fell against the U.S. dollar in early trade following a cut in the official cash rate by 0.5 point to 5.0 percent by the Reserve Bank of Australia.
But the Aussie later recovered due to short-covering and talk of buying by a Chinese bank, dealers said.
The Australian dollar stood at around $0.7462/67 at 0343 GMT after falling as low as around $0.7395 in early trade.
The dollar closed at 118.35/40 yen and 1.8375/85 marks in New York on Tuesday.
